Cc: legal@aperturesys.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Reserved capacity term & staggered ramp — Aperture Systems

Hi Simon,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great conversation and clear signals that Dedicated capacity is the right path for your production inference needs. Attached is a short workbook (Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Scenarios_v3.pdf) with three reserved-commit options (12/24/36 months) plus a couple of ramp schedules we think work well for enterprise customers that want predictable unit economics while avoiding large up-front utilization risk.

Quick summary:
- 12mo: higher unit price, minimal ramp flexibility; best if you’re confident on rapid product adoption.
- 24mo: middle ground on price, allows a 3–6 month staged capacity start to reduce initial ops/cost exposure.
- 36mo: deepest discount but requires a more structured stagger (quarterly increases) and a higher minimum commit.

Two things I need from you to make a firm SOW/quote:
1) Preferred commit term (12/24/36).
2) Proposed go-live window for first tranche of capacity (you mentioned mid-May).

If it helps, Neha has modeled a 24-month plan with a 60/100 GPU slot pool (committed/burst) and a staged ramp that starts at 20% capacity for months 1–3, 60% for months 4–6, then full commit after month 7. That keeps your up-front spend low while giving throughput guarantees once you ramp.

I’ll loop Jordan in to call out billing cadence and SLA language we should include.

Next steps: if you can confirm term and preferred start week by Friday, I’ll circulate a draft SOW for legal review.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@aperturesys.com>

Hi Rishi,

Appreciate the workbook — quick notes after a read with the engineering and finance leads: we like the 24mo middle path but have three clarifying questions before we sign off:

1) Throughput guarantees: can you convert the slot counts (GPU pools) into a tokens/sec or requests/sec SLA baseline? Engineering wants a hard floor we can rely on for tail-latency-sensitive endpoints.
2) Start date: mid-May is fine, but procurement needs a clear staggered start schedule and an invoice schedule that matches our quarterly budget windows. We prefer a 3-stage ramp (20% / 50% / 100%) with the second stage hitting by month 4.
3) Pricing: what incremental discount do we see if we commit to a 24mo but add an early-payment (annual upfront) clause? Would that approach give us near-36mo economics without the long-term lock?

Also forwarding to legal for any standard SOC/SLA addenda. If you can call out how Redwood treats queued requests during ramp (do you throttle, queue, or route to hosted fallback), that will inform our architecture.

Simon
VP Product
Aperture Systems

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@aperturesys.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity term & staggered ramp — Aperture Systems

Simon — thanks, great questions. Answers inline and I attached an updated scenarios PDF with numbers calculated for a 24-month model.

1) Throughput guarantees (24mo illustrative):
- Committed pool: 60 GPU slots (baseline) delivering a sustained inference throughput of ~18k tokens/sec aggregate (depends on model/seq length; see table in PDF).
- Burst pool: additional 40 GPU slots for peak traffic; Redwood routes to burst capacity when latency SLOs are at risk.
- SLA: we can commit to a 99.5% availability for committed capacity and a best-effort for burst with automated fallback to our hosted tier if Dedicated capacity is saturated. We can include a credits schedule (per 0.1% below SLO) in the SOW.

2) Staggered start: we can formalize the 3-stage ramp you prefer: 20% (month 0–3), 50% (month 4–6), 100% (month 7 onward). Start week: currently we have capacity availability beginning the week of 11 May 2026.

3) Pricing / early-payment:
- Base 24mo upfront-billed annually: ~8% discount vs monthly billing.
- 24mo with full annual prepay (payment at contract start for each 12mo tranche): additional 6% additive discount.
- 36mo baseline vs 24mo+prepay: door-step difference ~2–4% (depends on total commit). In short: prepaying for 12-month increments gets you most of the 36mo economics without the longer lock.

About queued requests: Redwood will accept and queue requests up to the committed concurrency; if queue depth grows beyond configured thresholds we will either route to hosted fallback (if you opt in) or return a 429 with an explicit retry-after. We recommend enabling hosted-fallback for peak reliability during the first 2 quarters of ramp.

I’ve included a sample invoice cadence in the PDF and highlighted the credits schedule that Jordan will call out for legal.

— Rishi

Quick legal/billing notes:
- We can support the 3-stage ramp and will capture the staggered start dates in the SOW milestone table.
- SLA credits: Jordan notes we typically cap cumulative credits at 30% of monthly committed fees over any 12mo window. If Aperture needs a higher cap we can discuss as an exception, but would need to align on remedies and monitoring hooks.
- Invoice cadence: Redwood can invoice annually upfront (12mo blocks), or quarterly-in-advance. For Aperture’s budget profile, annual upfront with the additional prepay discount looks like the best value.

I’ll review the PDF and return a redline for the SOW. Once we have term confirmation from Aperture, legal will push the draft to DocuSign.

Rishi / Jordan / Neha,

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — that clarifies most of the open items. Aperture’s procurement & finance teams convened and we have a preferred path:

- Term: 24 months
- Ramp: 3-stage (20% / 50% / 100%) with the second stage targeted to land by month 4; first tranche to begin the week of 11 May 2026.
- Billing: annual upfront for the first 12 months (we will prepay at contract signature), then quarterly in-advance for year two.

Please circulate the SOW and an invoice for the first 12mo prepayment. We aim to complete signatures and payment by the end of April to hit the May start.

Simon
